units.zh: 太祖武皇帝，諱克用，本姓朱耶氏，其先隴右金城人也。
units.en: The Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, personal name Keyong, was born of the Zhuye clan; his ancestors came from Jincheng in Longyou.
units.literal: Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, taboo name Keyong, originally surnamed Zhuye; his forebears were men of Jincheng in Longyou.

units.zh: 始祖拔野，唐貞觀中為墨離軍使，從太宗討高麗、薛延陁有功，為金方道副都護，因家於瓜州。
units.en: The founding ancestor Baye served as Mori Army commissioner under Zhenguan; he followed Taizong against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo, was rewarded as deputy protector of the Jin-fang Circuit, and settled his family at Guazhou.
units.literal: Founding ancestor Baye, in Tang Zhenguan served as Mori Army commissioner; following Taizong in campaigns against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo he had merit, was made Deputy Protector-General of the Jin-fang Circuit, and took residence at Guazhou.

units.zh: 太宗平薛延陁諸部，於安西、北庭置都護屬之，分同羅、仆骨之人，置沙陁都督府。
units.en: After Taizong subdued the Xueyantuo, he set protectors at Anxi and Beiting, assigned the Tongluo and Pugu to them, and founded the Shatuo Chief Commandery.
units.literal: Taizong pacified the Xueyantuo tribes, placed protectors at Anxi and Beiting subject to them, divided the Tongluo and Pugu peoples, and established the Shatuo Chief Commandery.

units.zh: 蓋北庭有磧曰沙陁，故因以為名焉。
units.en: A desert tract at Beiting was called Shatuo, and the name followed from that.
units.literal: For Beiting had a desert tract called Shatuo, hence the name.

units.zh: 永徽中，以拔野為都督，其後子孫五世相承。
units.en: Under Yonghui, Baye became chief; five generations of his line succeeded one another.
units.literal: In Yonghui, Baye was made chief; thereafter descendants held the post for five generations in succession.

units.zh: 曾祖盡忠，貞元中，繼為沙陀府都督。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jingzhong became Shatuo prefectural chief in the Zhenyuan era.
units.literal: Great-grandfather Jingzhong, in Zhenyuan, succeeded as Shatuo prefectural chief.

units.zh: 既而為吐蕃所陷，乃舉其族七千帳徙於甘州。
units.en: The Tibetans soon overran him; he led seven thousand tents of his clan to relocate at Ganzhou.
units.literal: Soon after he was trapped by the Tibetans; he then moved his clan, seven thousand tents, to Ganzhou.

units.zh: 盡忠尋率部眾三萬東奔，俄而吐蕃追兵大至，盡忠戰歿。
units.en: Jingzhong soon fled east with thirty thousand followers; Tibetan pursuit caught up and he fell in battle.
units.literal: Jingzhong soon led thirty thousand of his following east in flight; presently Tibetan pursuers came in force and Jingzhong died in battle.

units.zh: 祖執宜，即盡忠之長子也，收合餘眾，至於靈州，德宗命為陰山府都督。
units.en: His grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, rallied the survivors, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.
units.literal: Grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, gathered the remnant following, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong appointed him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.

units.zh: 元和初，入為金吾將軍，遷蔚州刺史、代北行營招撫使。
units.en: Early in Yuanhe he became a Golden Crow general, then prefect of Wei and pacification commissioner for the northern Dai frontier.
units.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he entered court as Golden Crow general, was transferred to prefect of Wei, and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·沙陀傳》：元和三年，盡忠款靈州塞，詔處其部鹽州置陰山府，以執宜為府兵馬使。
units.en: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》 says: In Yuanhe 3 Jingzhong came in at Lingzhou; the court settled his people at Yanzhou as Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhiyi its horse commissioner.
units.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》: In Yuanhe year 3 Jingzhong submitted at the Lingzhou pass; an edict settled his tribe at Yanzhou and established Yinshan Prefecture, making Zhiyi prefectural horse commissioner.

units.zh: 朝長安，授特進、金吾衛將軍。
units.en: At Chang'an he received Special Advancement and a post in the Golden Crow Guard.
units.literal: He attended court at Chang'an and was given Special Advancement and general of the Golden Crow Guard.

units.zh: 從攻鎮州，進蔚州刺史。
units.en: He took part in the Zhenzhou campaign and was promoted to Wei prefect.
units.literal: Following the attack on Zhen prefecture, he was advanced to prefect of Wei.

units.zh: 破吳元濟，授檢校刑部尚書。
units.en: After Wu Yuanji was broken he received the acting post of Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Defeating Wu Yuanji, he was made acting Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 長慶初，破賊深州，入朝留宿衛，拜金吾衛將軍。
units.en: Early in Changqing he crushed rebels at Shenzhou, stayed at court on palace guard duty, and became a Golden Crow Guard general.
units.literal: At the start of Changqing he defeated bandits at Shen prefecture, entered court and remained on palace guard, and was made general of the Golden Crow Guard.

units.zh: 太和中，授陰山府都督、代北行營招撫使。）〉
units.en: Under Taihe he was named governor of Yinshan Prefecture and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉
units.literal: In Taihe he was given Yinshan Prefecture governorship and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為昭烈皇帝，廟號懿祖。
units.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Zhaolie with temple name Ancestor Yi.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaolie, temple name Ancestor Yi.

units.zh: 烈考國昌，本名赤心，唐朔州刺史。
units.en: His father Guochang, born Chixin, had been Tang prefect of Shuo.
units.literal: His stern father Guochang, original name Chixin, was Tang prefect of Shuo.

units.zh: 咸通中，討龐勳有功，入為金吾上將軍，賜姓李氏，名國昌，
units.en: Under Xiantong he helped crush Pang Xun, entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, and received the imperial surname Li and the name Guochang,
units.literal: In Xiantong, campaigning against Pang Xun with merit, he entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, was granted the surname Li and the name Guochang,

units.zh: 〈（代州有《唐故龍武軍統軍檢校司徒贈太保隴四李公神道碑》云：公諱國昌，字德興。）〉
units.en: (A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉
units.literal: (At Dai prefecture there is the 《Stele of the Late Tang Longwu Army Commander-in-Chief, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi, Lord Li》 saying: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉

units.zh: 仍係鄭王房。
units.en: and he was entered in the genealogical line of the Prince of Zheng.
units.literal: and he was enrolled in the Prince of Zheng branch.

units.zh: 出為振武節度使，尋為吐渾所襲，退保於神武川。
units.en: He was posted as Zhenwu military commissioner; the Tuyuhun soon struck, and he fell back to Shenwu River.
units.literal: He went out as Zhenwu military commissioner; soon the Tuyuhun attacked and he withdrew to hold Shenwu River.

units.zh: 及武皇鎮太原，表為代北軍節度使。
units.en: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized Guochang as military commissioner of the northern Dai army.
units.literal: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized him as northern-campaign military commissioner.

units.zh: 中和三年薨。
units.en: He died in Zhonghe 3.
units.literal: He died in the third year of Zhonghe.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為文皇，廟號獻祖。
units.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Wen with temple name Ancestor Xian.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, temple name Ancestor Xian.

units.zh: 武皇即獻祖之第三子也。
units.en: Wuhuang was the third son of Ancestor Xian.
units.literal: Wuhuang was Ancestor Xian's third son.

units.zh: 母秦氏，以大中十年丙子歲九月二十二日，生於神武川之新城。
units.en: His mother was Lady Qin; he was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month, bingzi year of Dazhong 10, at New City on Shenwu River.
units.literal: His mother was the Lady Qin; on the twenty-second day of the ninth month of the bingzi year of Dazhong 10 he was born at New City on Shenwu River.

units.zh: 在妊十三月，載誕之際，母艱危者竟夕。
units.en: The pregnancy lasted thirteen months; on the night he was born his mother hovered between life and death.
units.literal: She carried him thirteen months; at the moment of birth the mother was in grave peril the whole night.

units.zh: 族人憂駭，市藥於雁門，遇神叟告曰：「非巫醫所及，可馳歸，盡率部人，被甲持旄，擊鉦鼓，躍馬大噪，環所居三周而止。」
units.en: Kinfolk in panic sought medicine at Yanmen; a divine old man told them, "No doctor can help—gallop home, arm every tribesman with banners, beat gongs and drums, ride shouting, and circle the house three times."
units.literal: The clansmen were alarmed and bought medicine at Yanmen; they met a divine old man who said: "This is beyond shamans and physicians—ride back at once, muster all your tribesmen in armor with banners, strike gongs and drums, gallop and shout loudly, and circle the dwelling three times, then stop."

units.zh: 族人如其教，果無恙而生。
units.en: They did so, and mother and child came through safely.
units.literal: The clansmen did as instructed and he was indeed born unharmed.

units.zh: 是時，虹光燭室，白氣充庭，井水暴溢。
units.en: A rainbow filled the room, white mist flooded the courtyard, and the well burst its banks.
units.literal: At that time a rainbow lit the chamber, white vapor filled the courtyard, and the well water suddenly overflowed.

units.zh: 武皇始言，喜軍中語，齠齔善騎射，與儕類馳騁嬉戲，必出其右。
units.en: From his first words he loved camp speech; as a boy he rode and shot superbly and always beat his playmates in their games.
units.literal: When Wuhuang first spoke he delighted in army talk; in childhood he excelled at riding and archery; racing and playing with his peers he always came out ahead.

units.zh: 年十三，見雙鳧翔於空，射之連中，眾皆臣伏。
units.en: At thirteen he brought down two mandarin ducks in one flight; onlookers bowed in awe.
units.literal: At thirteen he saw paired mandarin ducks flying in the sky, shot them both in succession, and all submitted in awe.

units.zh: 新城北有毗沙天王祠，祠前井一日沸溢，武皇因持酒而奠曰：「予有尊主濟民之志，無何井溢，故未察其禍福，惟天王若有神奇，可與仆交談。」
units.en: North of New City stood a Vaisravana shrine whose well one day boiled over; Wuhuang poured a libation and said, "I mean to serve my sovereign and save the people; this well has burst without warning, so I cannot read the omen—Heavenly King, if you have power, speak with me."
units.literal: North of New City was a shrine to the Vaisravana Heavenly King; one day the well before the shrine boiled over; Wuhuang therefore held wine and made offering, saying: "I have the will to honor the ruler and succor the people; suddenly the well overflows, so I have not yet discerned fortune or misfortune; if the Heavenly King has divine power, you may speak with your servant."

units.zh: 奠酒未已，有神人被金甲持戈，隱然出於壁間，見者大驚走，惟武皇從容而退，由是益自負。
units.en: Before the cup was drained an armored figure with a spear seemed to step from the wall; all fled in terror while Wuhuang walked away calmly, and his pride only grew.
units.literal: Before the offering was finished a divine man in golden armor with a spear faintly emerged from the wall; those who saw it fled in terror, only Wuhuang withdrew at ease, and from this he grew still prouder.

units.zh: 獻祖之討龐勳也，武皇年十五，從征，摧鋒陷陣，出諸將之右，軍中目為「飛虎子」。
units.en: At fifteen Wuhuang followed Ancestor Xian against Pang Xun, led every charge, and outshone the generals; the troops nicknamed him the "Flying Tiger Cub."
units.literal: When Ancestor Xian campaigned against Pang Xun, Wuhuang was fifteen; he followed the expedition, smashed the van and broke formations, surpassing the generals; the army called him "Flying Tiger Cub."

units.zh: 賊平，獻祖授振武節度使，武皇為雲中牙將。
units.en: After the rebels fell Ancestor Xian received Zhenwu and Wuhuang became an adjutant at Yunzhong.
units.literal: When the bandits were pacified Ancestor Xian was made Zhenwu military commissioner and Wuhuang became a Yunzhong adjutant.

units.zh: 嘗在雲中，宿於別館，擁妓醉寢，有俠兒持刃欲害武皇；
units.en: Once in Yunzhong he slept drunk with courtesans in a side lodge while an assassin crept in with a blade;
units.literal: Once at Yunzhong he lodged at a side hall, embraced courtesans and slept drunk; a bravo drew a blade intending to kill Wuhuang;

units.zh: 及突入曲室，但見烈火熾赫於帳中，俠兒駭異而退。
units.en: but inside the tent blazed with fire; the man fled in horror.
units.literal: when he burst into the inner room he saw only fierce flames blazing in the tent; the bravo fled in terror.

units.zh: 又嘗與達靼部人角勝，達靼指雙雕於空曰：「公能一發中否？」
units.en: Another time he competed with Tatars who pointed to two eagles aloft and asked, "Can you drop both with one arrow?"
units.literal: Again he once matched skill with men of the Tatar tribes; a Tatar pointed to paired eagles in the sky and said: "Can my lord bring them down with one shot?"

units.zh: 武皇即彎弧發矢，連貫雙雕，邊人拜伏。
units.en: He bent his bow and struck both; the border people prostrated themselves.
units.literal: Wuhuang at once bent the bow and loosed; he pierced both eagles in succession and the border people bowed in submission.

units.zh: 及壯，為雲中守捉使，事防禦使支謨，與同列晨集廨舍，因戲升郡閣，踞謨之座，謨亦不敢詰。
units.en: As a man he was Yunzhong garrison commander under defense commissioner Zhi Mo; one morning he and his fellows climbed the prefectural tower for sport and sprawled on Mo's seat, and Mo did not dare rebuke him.
units.literal: When grown he was Yunzhong frontier garrison commander, serving defense commissioner Zhi Mo; with his peers he gathered at dawn in the yamen and in sport climbed the prefectural tower and sat on Mo's seat; Mo also dared not reprove him.

units.zh: 乾符三年，朝廷以段文楚為代北水陸發運、雲州防禦使。
units.en: In Qianfu 3 the court appointed Duan Wenchu commissioner of northern transport and Yunzhou defense.
units.literal: In Qianfu year 3 the court made Duan Wenchu northern land-and-water transport commissioner and Yunzhou defense commissioner.

units.zh: 時歲薦饑，文楚稍削軍食，諸軍鹹怨。
units.en: Famine struck again; Wenchu trimmed rations and the whole army seethed.
units.literal: That year famine returned; Wenchu slightly reduced army rations and all the troops resented it.

units.zh: 武皇為雲中防邊督將，部下爭訴以軍食不充，邊校程懷素、王行審、蓋寓、李存璋、薛鐵山、康君立等，即擁武皇入雲州，眾且萬人，營於鬥雞台，城中械文楚出，以應於外。
units.en: Wuhuang, as Yunzhong frontier superintendent, heard endless complaints of short rations; Cheng Huaisu, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli, and other frontier officers then forced him into Yunzhou with nearly ten thousand men at Cockfight Terrace while the city handed Wenchu over to them.
units.literal: Wuhuang was Yunzhong frontier superintendent; his men complained that rations were short; frontier officers Cheng Huaisu, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli, and others at once escorted Wuhuang into Yunzhou—nearly ten thousand men—encamped at Cockfight Terrace, and the city bound Wenchu and sent him out to answer them.

units.zh: 諸將列狀以聞，請授武皇旄鉞，朝廷不允，征諸道兵以討之。
units.en: The officers memorialized jointly for Wuhuang to receive the baton of command; the court refused and mobilized every circuit against them.
units.literal: The generals submitted a joint memorial asking that Wuhuang be granted the command baton; the court refused and raised troops from all circuits to punish them.

units.zh: 乾符五年，黃巢渡江，其勢滋蔓，天子乃悟其事，以武皇為大同軍節度使、檢校工部尚書。
units.en: In Qianfu 5 Huang Chao crossed the river and his strength swelled; the emperor then grasped the situation and made Wuhuang Datong military commissioner and acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: In Qianfu year 5 Huang Chao crossed the Yangzi and his power spread; the Son of Heaven then understood the matter and made Wuhuang Datong military commissioner and acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 冬，獻祖出師討党項，吐渾赫連鐸乘虛陷振武，舉族為吐渾所擄。
units.en: That winter Ancestor Xian marched against the Tangut; Helian Duo of the Tuyuhun struck Zhenwu in his absence and carried off the whole clan.
units.literal: Winter: Ancestor Xian marched to campaign against the Tangut; the Tuyuhun Helian Duo seized the chance and took Zhenwu; the whole clan was captured by the Tuyuhun.

units.zh: 武皇至定邊軍迎獻祖歸雲州，雲州守將拒關不納。
units.en: Wuhuang met Ancestor Xian at Dingbian and tried to return to Yunzhou, but the garrison barred the gates.
units.literal: Wuhuang went to Dingbian army to welcome Ancestor Xian back to Yunzhou; Yunzhou's garrison commander shut the pass and would not admit them.

units.zh: 武皇略蔚、朔之地，得三千人，屯神武川之新城。
units.en: Wuhuang swept Wei and Shuo, raised three thousand men, and camped at New City on Shenwu River.
units.literal: Wuhuang raided Wei and Shuo, gathered three thousand men, and encamped at New City on Shenwu River.

units.zh: 赫邊鐸晝夜攻圍，武皇昆弟三人四面應賊，俄而獻祖自蔚州引軍至，吐渾退走，自是軍勢復振。
units.en: Helian Duo pressed the siege without pause; Wuhuang and his three brothers fought on every side until Ancestor Xian marched from Weizhou and the Tuyuhun pulled back; their power revived.
units.literal: Helian Duo besieged day and night; Wuhuang and his three brothers answered the enemy on four sides; presently Ancestor Xian led troops from Wei prefecture; the Tuyuhun withdrew, and from this the army's strength revived.

units.zh: 天子以赫連鐸為大同軍節度使，仍命進軍以討武皇。
units.en: The court named Helian Duo Datong commissioner and ordered him to march on Wuhuang.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven made Helian Duo Datong military commissioner and still ordered advance to campaign against Wuhuang.

units.zh: 乾符六年春，朝廷以昭義節度使李鈞充北面招討使，將上黨、太原之師過石嶺關，屯於代州，與幽州李可舉會赫連鐸同攻蔚州。
units.en: In spring of Qianfu 6 Li Jun of Zhaoyi was made northern commander-in-chief; he led Shangdang and Taiyuan forces through Shiling Pass to Dai, and with Li Keju of Youzhou and Helian Duo besieged Weizhou.
units.literal: Spring of Qianfu year 6: the court made Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Jun northern campaign commander-in-chief, leading Shangdang and Taiyuan troops through Shiling Pass to encamp at Dai prefecture, and with Youzhou's Li Keju joined Helian Duo to attack Weizhou together.

units.zh: 獻祖以一軍禦之，武皇以一軍南抵遮虜城以拒李鈞。
units.en: Ancestor Xian met them with one wing; Wuhuang took another south to Zhelu Fort to stop Li Jun.
units.literal: Ancestor Xian held them with one army; Wuhuang with one army went south to Zhelu Fort to block Li Jun.

units.zh: 是冬大雪，弓弩弦折，南軍苦寒，臨戰大敗，奔歸代州，李鈞中流矢而卒。
units.en: Heavy snow that winter snapped every bowstring; the southern force froze, broke in battle, fled to Dai, and Li Jun died of an arrow wound.
units.literal: That winter heavy snow snapped bowstrings; the southern army suffered bitter cold, was utterly defeated in battle, fled back to Dai, and Li Jun died of an arrow wound.

units.zh: 廣明元年春，天子復命元帥李涿率兵數萬屯代州。
units.en: In spring of Guangming 1 the emperor again sent Marshal Li Zhuo with tens of thousands to camp at Dai.
units.literal: Spring of Guangming year 1: the Son of Heaven again ordered marshal Li Zhuo to lead tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Dai.

units.zh: 武皇令軍使傅文達起兵於蔚州，朔州刺史高文集與薛葛、安慶等部將縛文達送於李涿。
units.en: Wuhuang had Fu Wenda raise troops at Weizhou; Shuo prefect Gao Wenji and officers Xue Ge and An Qing bound Wenda and delivered him to Li Zhuo.
units.literal: Wuhuang ordered army commissioner Fu Wenda to raise troops at Weizhou; Shuo prefect Gao Wenji with subordinates Xue Ge, An Qing, and others bound Wenda and sent him to Li Zhuo.

units.zh: 六月，李涿引大軍攻蔚州，獻祖戰不利，乃率其族奔於達靼部。
units.en: In the sixth month Li Zhuo assaulted Weizhou; Ancestor Xian was beaten and fled with his clan to the Tatars.
units.literal: Sixth month: Li Zhuo led a great army to attack Weizhou; Ancestor Xian fought unfavorably and then led his clan in flight to the Tatar tribes.

units.zh: 居數月，吐渾赫連鐸密遣人賂達靼以離間獻祖，既而漸生猜阻。
units.en: Months later Helian Duo bribed the Tatars to turn against Ancestor Xian, and distrust slowly took hold.
units.literal: After several months the Tuyuhun Helian Duo secretly sent men to bribe the Tatars to estrange Ancestor Xian, and suspicion gradually grew.

units.zh: 武皇知之，每召其豪右射獵於野，或與之百步馳射馬鞭，或以懸針樹葉為的，中之如神，由是部人心伏，不敢竊發。
units.en: Wuhuang saw it; he hunted with their leaders, matched them shooting horsewhips at a hundred paces, or pinned hanging needles and leaves—and never missed; the tribes submitted in awe and dared not plot.
units.literal: Wuhuang knew it; he often summoned their chieftains to hunt in the wild, or raced them at a hundred paces shooting at horsewhips, or used hanging needles and tree leaves as targets and hit them like a spirit; thereby the tribes submitted in heart and dared not act secretly.

units.zh: 俄而黃巢自江、淮北渡，武皇椎牛釃酒，饗其酋首。
units.en: When Huang Chao crossed north from the Jiang-Huai region, Wuhuang slaughtered oxen and poured wine to feast the Tatar chiefs.
units.literal: Presently Huang Chao crossed north from south of the Yangzi and Huai; Wuhuang slaughtered oxen and poured wine to feast their chiefs.

units.zh: 酒酣，諭之曰：「予父子為賊臣讒間，報國無由。
units.en: Deep in his cups he told them, "Slander cut my father and me off from the throne—we could not serve the realm.
units.literal: When the wine was deep he admonished them, saying: "My father and I were estranged by slanderous ministers and had no way to serve the state.

units.zh: 今聞黃巢北犯江、淮，必為中原之患。
units.en: Now Huang Chao drives north along the Yangzi and Huai and will ravage the heartland.
units.literal: Now I hear Huang Chao is marching north against the Yangzi and Huai and will surely become a scourge to the central plains.

units.zh: 一日天子赦宥，有詔征兵，仆與公等向南而定天下，是予心也。
units.en: When the emperor pardons us and calls for armies, I mean to march south with you and settle the empire.
units.literal: If one day the Son of Heaven pardons and an edict summons troops, your servant with you will march south and settle the realm—that is my heart.

units.zh: 人生世間，光景幾何，曷能終老沙堆中哉！
units.en: Life is brief—who wants to die in the sand?
units.literal: How long is a man's life in this world—how can we end our days in desert sands!

units.zh: 公等勉之。」
units.en: Take heart, all of you."
units.literal: Do your best, gentlemen."

units.zh: 達靼知無留意，皆釋然無間。
units.en: Seeing he would not linger, the Tatars put aside suspicion.
units.literal: The Tatars knew he had no mind to stay and all relaxed without estrangement.

units.zh: 是歲十一月，黃巢寇潼關，天子令河東監軍陳景思為代北起軍使，收兵破賊。
units.en: In the eleventh month Huang Chao threatened Tong Pass; the emperor made Chen Jingsi of Hedong northern recruiting commissioner to raise troops against him.
units.literal: That year, eleventh month: Huang Chao threatened Tong Pass; the Son of Heaven ordered Hedong eunuch commissioner Chen Jingsi northern recruiting commissioner to gather troops and break the bandits.

units.zh: 十二月，黃巢犯長安，僖宗幸蜀，陳景思與李友金發沙陁諸部五千騎南赴京師。
units.en: In the twelfth month Huang Chao took Chang'an; Xizong fled to Shu; Chen Jingsi and Li Youjin led five thousand Shatuo horsemen south to the capital.
units.literal: Twelfth month: Huang Chao entered Chang'an; Emperor Xizong fled to Shu; Chen Jingsi and Li Youjin led five thousand Shatuo cavalry south toward the capital.

units.zh: 友金即武皇之族父也。
units.en: Youjin was Wuhuang's kinsman on his father's side.
units.literal: Youjin was Wuhuang's clansman uncle.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：友金初與高文集並降於李琢，故得與陳景思南赴京師。）〉
units.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Youjin had surrendered with Gao Wenji to Li Zhuo, which let him join Chen Jingsi's march south.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Youjin had first surrendered with Gao Wenji to Li Zhuo, and therefore could march south with Chen Jingsi.)〉

units.zh: 中和元年二月，友金軍至絳州，將渡河，刺史瞿稹謂陳景思曰：「巢賊方盛，不如且還代北，徐圖利害。」
units.en: In the second month of Zhonghe 1 Youjin reached Jiangzhou to cross the river; Qu Zhi told Chen Jingsi, "Chao is still rampant—fall back to Dai for now and choose your moment."
units.literal: Second month, Zhonghe year 1: Youjin's army reached Jiang prefecture and was about to cross the river; prefect Qu Zhi said to Chen Jingsi: "The Chao bandits are still strong; better for now to return to Dai and weigh advantage slowly."

units.zh: 四月，友金旋軍雁門，瞿稹至代州，半月之間，募兵三萬，營於崞縣之西。
units.en: In the fourth month Youjin withdrew to Yanmen; Qu Zhi reached Dai and raised thirty thousand men west of Guo in a fortnight.
units.literal: Fourth month: Youjin turned the army to Yanmen; Qu Zhi reached Dai prefecture; within half a month he recruited thirty thousand troops and encamped west of Guo county.

units.zh: 其軍皆北邊五部之眾，不閑軍法，瞿正、李友金不能制。
units.en: They were tribesmen of the five northern confederacies, untrained in drill; neither Qu Zheng nor Li Youjin could hold them.
units.literal: The army was all men of the five northern tribes, unskilled in military law; Qu Zheng and Li Youjin could not control them.

units.zh: 友金謂景思曰：「興大眾，成大事，當威名素著，則可以伏人。
units.en: Youjin told Jingsi, "A great host needs a name men already fear.
units.literal: Youjin said to Jingsi: "To raise a great host and accomplish a great deed one must already possess renown, then one can overawe men.

units.zh: 今軍雖數萬，苟無善帥，進亦無功。
units.en: Tens of thousands without a proven leader will march nowhere.
units.literal: Now though the army numbers tens of thousands, without a good commander advance will also be fruitless.

units.zh: 吾兄李司徒父子，去歲獲罪於國家，今寄北部，雄武之略，為眾所推。
units.en: My kinsman Minister Li and his son offended the court last year and shelter in the north; everyone trusts their martial genius.
units.literal: My elder brother Minister Li and his son last year offended the state and now lodge in the north; their bold strategy is what the masses push forward.

units.zh: 若驃騎急奏召還，代北之人，一麾響應，則妖賊不足平也。」
units.en: Summon them by urgent memorial and every northerner will rally—Chao will fall easily."
units.literal: If the commissioner urgently memorializes to recall them, the men of Dai will answer at one wave of the banner, and the demon bandits will not be hard to pacify."

units.zh: 景思然之，促奏行在。
units.en: Jingsi agreed and rushed word to the court in exile.
units.literal: Jingsi agreed and hurried a memorial to the traveling court.

units.zh: 天子乃以武皇為雁門節度使，仍令以本軍討賊。
units.en: The emperor then named Wuhuang Yanmen military commissioner and ordered his troops against the rebels.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven then made Wuhuang Yanmen military commissioner and still ordered his army to campaign against the bandits.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·王重榮傳》：重榮懼黃巢復振，憂之，與復光計，復光曰：「我世與李克用共憂患，其人忠不顧難，死義如己，若乞師焉，事蔑不濟。」
units.en: (The 《New Tang History · Wang Chongrong Biography》 says Chongrong dreaded Chao's return and consulted Fuguang, who said, "Our houses and Li Keyong have shared peril for generations; he is loyal, fearless, and treats another's death as his own—ask him for troops and you cannot fail."
units.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Wang Chongrong Biography》: Chongrong feared Huang Chao would revive and was anxious; with Fuguang he took counsel; Fuguang said: "My house and Li Keyong have shared hardship for generations; the man is loyal and heedless of danger, treats death as his own—if you beg troops of him, nothing will fail."

units.zh: 乃遣使者約連和。）〉
units.en: Envoys were sent to ally with him.)〉
units.literal: He then sent envoys to arrange alliance.)〉

units.zh: 李友金發五百騎齎詔召武皇於達靼，武皇即率達靼諸部萬人趨雁門。
units.en: Li Youjin sent five hundred horsemen with the edict to fetch Wuhuang from the Tatars; he led ten thousand Tatar riders straight for Yanmen.
units.literal: Li Youjin sent five hundred cavalry bearing the edict to summon Wuhuang from the Tatars; Wuhuang at once led ten thousand men of the Tatar tribes toward Yanmen.

units.zh: 五月，整兵二萬，南向京師。
units.en: In the fifth month he gathered twenty thousand men and marched south on the capital.
units.literal: Fifth month: he mustered twenty thousand troops and marched south toward the capital.

units.zh: 太原鄭從讜以兵守石嶺關，武皇乃引軍出他道；
units.en: Zheng Congdang of Taiyuan blocked Shiling Pass; Wuhuang detoured;
units.literal: Taiyuan's Zheng Congdang held troops at Shiling Pass; Wuhuang therefore led the army by another route;

units.zh: 至太原城下，會大雨，班師於雁門。
units.en: but heavy rain at Taiyuan forced him back to Yanmen.
units.literal: reaching below Taiyuan city he met great rain and withdrew the army to Yanmen.

units.zh: 中和二年八月，獻祖自達靼部率其族歸代州。
units.en: In the eighth month of Zhonghe 2 Ancestor Xian brought his clan home from the Tatars to Dai.
units.literal: Eighth month, Zhonghe year 2: Ancestor Xian led his clan back from the Tatar tribes to Dai prefecture.

units.zh: 十月，武皇率忻、代、蔚、朔、達靼之軍三萬五千騎赴難於京師。
units.en: In the tenth month Wuhuang marched south with thirty-five thousand horse from Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and the Tatars to save the court.
units.literal: Tenth month: Wuhuang led thirty-five thousand cavalry of Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and the Tatars south to relieve the capital.

units.zh: 先移檄太原，鄭從讜拒關不納，武皇以兵擊之，進軍至城下，遣人齎幣馬遺從讜；
units.en: He announced his coming at Taiyuan; Congdang barred the pass; Wuhuang assaulted the city and sent gifts of silk and horses;
units.literal: First he sent a proclamation to Taiyuan; Zheng Congdang shut the pass and would not admit them; Wuhuang attacked with troops, advanced to below the wall, and sent men bearing gifts of silks and horses to Congdang;

units.zh: 從讜亦遣人饋武皇貨幣、饔餼、軍器。
units.en: Congdang replied with goods, food, and arms.
units.literal: Congdang also sent men presenting Wuhuang with goods, provisions, and weapons.

units.zh: 武皇南去，自陰地趨晉、絳。
units.en: Wuhuang turned south through Yindi toward Jin and Jiang.
units.literal: Wuhuang went south by the Yindi route toward Jin and Jiang.

units.zh: 十二月，武皇至河中。
units.en: In the twelfth month Wuhuang reached Hezhong.
units.literal: Twelfth month: Wuhuang reached Hezhong.

units.zh: 中和三年正月，晉國公王鐸承製授武皇東北面行營都統。
units.en: In the first month of Zhonghe 3 Wang Duo, Duke of Jin, appointed Wuhuang overall commander of the northeastern campaign by imperial order.
units.literal: First month, Zhonghe year 3: Jin State Duke Wang Duo, by imperial order, made Wuhuang overall commander of the northeastern campaign.

units.zh: 武皇令其弟克修領前鋒五百騎渡河視賊，黃巢遣將米重威齎重賂及偽詔以賜武皇；
units.en: He sent his brother Kexiu with five hundred vanguard horsemen to scout the rebels; Chao's general Mi Chongwei came with rich gifts and a forged edict;
units.literal: Wuhuang ordered his younger brother Kexiu to lead five hundred vanguard cavalry across the river to reconnoiter the bandits; Huang Chao sent the general Mi Chongwei bearing heavy bribes and a false edict to bestow on Wuhuang;

units.zh: 武皇納其賂以給諸將，燔其偽詔。
units.en: Wuhuang paid his officers from the bribes and burned the forged edict.
units.literal: Wuhuang took the bribes to supply the generals and burned the false edict.

units.zh: 是時，諸道勤王之師雲集京畿，然以賊勢尚熾，未敢爭鋒。
units.en: Every circuit had sent relief troops to the capital, but Chao was still too strong for anyone to close with him.
units.literal: At that time the relief armies of all circuits gathered thickly about the capital, yet because the bandit power was still fierce none dared contend at the spearpoint.

units.zh: 及武皇將至，賊帥相謂曰：「鴉兒軍至，當避其鋒。」
units.en: As Wuhuang drew near, the rebel commanders said among themselves: "The Crow-Son Army is here—we must give way to their attack."
units.literal: When Wuhuang was about to arrive, the bandit chiefs said to one another: "The Crow-Son Army is coming—we must avoid their edge."

units.zh: 武皇以兵自夏陽濟河。
units.en: Wuhuang crossed the Yellow River from Xiayang with his army.
units.literal: Wuhuang led his troops across the river from Xiayang.

units.zh: 二月，營於乾坑店。
units.en: In the second month he camped at Qiangeng Post.
units.literal: Second month, he encamped at Qiangeng Post.

units.zh: 黃巢大將尚讓、林言、王璠、趙璋等引軍十五萬屯於梁田坡。
units.en: Shang Rang, Lin Yan, Wang Fan, and Zhao Zhang, Huang Chao's chief generals, brought a hundred and fifty thousand men to Liangtian Slope.
units.literal: Huang Chao's great generals Shang Rang, Lin Yan, Wang Fan, and Zhao Zhang led a hundred and fifty thousand men and encamped at Liangtian Slope.

units.zh: 翌日，大軍合戰，自午及晡，巢賊大敗。
units.en: The next day the armies fought from noon until dusk and Huang Chao's forces were routed.
units.literal: The next day the armies joined battle; from noon until the second watch the Chao bandits were utterly defeated.

units.zh: 是夜，賊眾遁據華州。
units.en: That night the rebels withdrew into Hua prefecture.
units.literal: That night the bandit host fled and held Hua prefecture.

units.zh: 武皇進軍圍之，巢弟黃鄴、黃揆固守。
units.en: Wuhuang pressed the siege while Huang Ye and Huang Kui, Huang Chao's brothers, defended the city.
units.literal: Wuhuang advanced to besiege it; Huang Chao's younger brothers Huang Ye and Huang Kui held firm.

units.zh: 三月，尚讓引大軍赴援，武皇率兵萬餘逆戰於零口，巢軍大敗，武皇進軍渭橋。
units.en: In the third month Shang Rang marched to relieve the city; Wuhuang met him at Lingkou with over ten thousand men, routed the Chao army, and advanced to Wei Bridge.
units.literal: Third month, Shang Rang led a great army to the relief; Wuhuang with more than ten thousand men met them in battle at Lingkou, the Chao army was crushed, and Wuhuang marched to Wei Bridge.

units.zh: 翌日，黃揆棄華州而遁。
units.en: The next day Huang Kui abandoned Hua and fled.
units.literal: The next day Huang Kui abandoned Hua prefecture and fled.

units.zh: 王鐸承製授武皇雁門節度使、檢校尚書左僕射。
units.en: Wang Duo, acting on imperial orders, made Wuhuang military commissioner of Yanmen and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: Wang Duo, acting on imperial commission, appointed Wuhuang military commissioner of Yanmen and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 四月，黃巢燔長安，收其餘眾，東走藍關。
units.en: In the fourth month Huang Chao burned Chang'an, rallied his survivors, and fled east through Lan Pass.
units.literal: Fourth month, Huang Chao burned Chang'an, gathered his remaining followers, and fled east through Lan Pass.

units.zh: 武皇時收京師。
units.en: Wuhuang was then taking control of the capital.
units.literal: Wuhuang was then recovering the capital.

units.zh: 七月，天子授武皇金紫光祿大夫、檢校左僕射、河東節度使。
units.en: In the seventh month the emperor named Wuhuang Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, honorary Left Vice Director, and military commissioner of Hedong.
units.literal: Seventh month, the Son of Heaven appointed Wuhuang Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, honorary Left Vice Director, and military commissioner of Hedong.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書·僖宗紀》：五月，製以雁門以北行營節度、忻代蔚朔等州觀察處置等使、檢校尚書左僕射、代州刺史、上柱國、食邑七百戶李克用檢校司空、同平章事兼太原尹、北京留守，充河東節度、管內觀察處置等使。
units.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang · Annals of Emperor Xizong》 records that in the fifth month Li Keyong—already campaign commissioner north of Yanmen and military commissioner of Xin, Dai, Wei, and Shuo—was promoted to Minister of Works, Tongping Grand Councilor, Grand Governor of Taiyuan, and full Hedong commissioner.)
units.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang · Annals of Emperor Xizong》 says: In the fifth month, by imperial edict, Li Keyong, campaign commissioner north of Yanmen, observation and disposition commissioner for Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and other prefectures, honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, prefect of Dai, Supreme Pillar of State, with a fief of seven hundred households, was made honorary Minister of Works, Tongping Grand Councilor, concurrently Grand Governor of Taiyuan and Beijing Protector, and military commissioner of Hedong with full authority over his circuit.)

units.zh: 《新唐書·沙陀傳》云：收京師功第一，進同中書門下平章事、隴西郡公。
units.en: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of the Shatuo》 adds that for leading the recovery of the capital he became Tongping Grand Councilor and Duke of Longxi.
units.literal: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of the Shatuo》 says: For first merit in recovering the capital he was advanced to Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi and Duke of Longxi.

units.zh: 未幾，以克用領河東節度。）〉
units.en: Soon afterward he took up the Hedong commission in full.)〉
units.literal: Before long Li Keyong was put in charge of the Hedong commission.)〉

units.zh: 是時，武皇既收長安，軍勢甚雄，諸侯之師皆畏之。
units.en: By then Wuhuang held Chang'an and his army was so powerful that the other warlords feared him.
units.literal: At that time Wuhuang had recovered Chang'an and his army was very strong; the armies of the other lords all feared him.

units.zh: 武皇一目微眇，故其時號為「獨眼龍」。
units.en: One of his eyes was weak, and men called him the "One-Eyed Dragon."
units.literal: Wuhuang had one eye slightly blind, and for that reason he was then called the "One-Eyed Dragon."

units.zh: 是月，武皇仗節赴鎮。
units.en: That month he set out for his post with the imperial baton of office.
units.literal: That month Wuhuang went to his commission bearing the imperial baton.

units.zh: 遣使報鄭從讜，請治裝歸朝。
units.en: He notified Zheng Congdang and asked him to make ready for the return to court.
units.literal: He sent envoys to inform Zheng Congdang and asked him to prepare to return to court.

units.zh: 武皇次於郊外，因往赴雁門寧覲獻祖。
units.en: He paused in the suburbs, then went to Yanmen to pay respects to Ancestor Xian.
units.literal: Wuhuang halted in the suburbs and then went to Yanmen to pay a reverent visit to his ancestor Xian.

units.zh: 八月，自雁門赴鎮河東，時年二十有八。
units.en: In the eighth month he left Yanmen for Hedong; he was twenty-eight years old.
units.literal: Eighth month, he left Yanmen for his Hedong commission; he was twenty-eight.

units.zh: 十一月，平潞州，表其弟克修為昭義節度使。
units.en: In the eleventh month he took Lu prefecture and asked that his brother Kexiu be made Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: Eleventh month, he pacified Lu prefecture and memorialized that his younger brother Kexiu be made military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 潞帥孟方立退保於邢州。
units.en: Meng Fangli, the Lu commander, fell back to defend Xing prefecture.
units.literal: The Lu commander Meng Fangli withdrew to hold Xing prefecture.

units.zh: 十二月，許帥田從異、汴帥朱溫、徐帥時溥、陳州刺史趙犨各遣使來告，以巢、蔡合從，凶鋒尚熾，請武皇共力討賊。
units.en: In the twelfth month Tian Congyi of Xu prefecture, Zhu Wen of Bian, Shi Pu of Xuzhou, and Zhao Chou of Chen each wrote that Huang Chao and the Cai rebels were allied and still dangerous, and begged Wuhuang to help destroy them.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Tian Congyi of Xu prefecture, Zhu Wen of Bian, Shi Pu of Xuzhou, and Zhao Chou, prefect of Chen, each sent envoys to report that Huang Chao and Cai had joined forces, their ferocity was still fierce, and to ask Wuhuang to join in exterminating the bandits.

units.zh: 中和四年春，武皇率蕃漢之師五萬，自澤、潞將下天井關；
units.en: In the spring of Zhonghe 4 Wuhuang led fifty thousand mixed Tartar and Chinese troops from Ze and Lu down on Tianjing Pass;
units.literal: Spring of the fourth year of Zhonghe, Wuhuang led fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops from Ze and Lu toward Tianjing Pass;

units.zh: 河陽節度使諸葛爽辭以河橋不完，乃屯兵於萬善。
units.en: Zhuge Shuang of Heyang said the river bridge was unfinished, so the army halted at Wanshan.
units.literal: the Hedong commissioner Zhuge Shuang pleaded that the Yellow River bridge was not complete, so the army encamped at Wanshan.

units.zh: 數日。
units.en: After several days,
units.literal: Several days passed.

units.zh: 移軍自河中南渡，趨汝、洛。
units.en: Wuhuang crossed the river from Hezhong and marched on Ru and Luo.
units.literal: he shifted the army, crossed south from Heyang, and pressed toward Ru and Luo.

units.zh: 四月，武皇合徐、汴之師破尚讓於太康，斬獲萬計，進攻賊於西華，賊將黃鄴棄營而遁。
units.en: In the fourth month, with the Xu and Bian armies, he crushed Shang Rang at Taikang, took tens of thousands of heads and captives, and drove on Xihua until Huang Ye abandoned his camp.
units.literal: Fourth month, Wuhuang combined with the Xu and Bian armies to defeat Shang Rang at Taikang, beheading and capturing tens of thousands, then attacked the bandits at Xihua; the bandit general Huang Ye abandoned camp and fled.

units.zh: 是夜大雨，巢營中驚亂，乃棄西華之壘，退營陳州北故陽裏。
units.en: That night heavy rain panicked Huang Chao's camp; they left Xihua and fell back to the old Yang quarter north of Chen.
units.literal: That night a great rain fell; Chao's camp was thrown into alarm, and they abandoned the Xihua fort and withdrew to the old Yang quarter north of Chen prefecture.

units.zh: 五月癸亥，大雨震電，平地水深數尺，賊營為水所漂而潰。
units.en: On guihai in the fifth month thunder and torrential rain flooded the plain several feet deep and washed the rebel camps away.
units.literal: On guihai of the fifth month, great rain, thunder, and lightning; the water on level ground was several feet deep, and the bandit camps were washed away and collapsed.

units.zh: 戊辰，武皇引軍營於中牟，大破賊於王滿渡。
units.en: On wuchen he encamped at Zhongmou and routed the rebels at Wangman Ford.
units.literal: On wuchen Wuhuang led the army to camp at Zhongmou and inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Wangman Ford.

units.zh: 庚午，巢賊大至，濟汴而北。
units.en: On gengwu Huang Chao brought up his main force and crossed the Bian River northward.
units.literal: On gengwu the Chao bandits came in force and crossed the Bian River going north.

units.zh: 是夜，復大雨，賊黨驚潰。
units.en: That night another storm broke the rebel ranks in panic.
units.literal: That night there was again great rain, and the bandit party panicked and broke.

units.zh: 武皇營於鄭州，賊眾分寇汴境。
units.en: Wuhuang camped at Zhengzhou while rebel detachments raided the Bian border.
units.literal: Wuhuang encamped at Zhengzhou; the bandit host split to raid the Bian frontier.

units.zh: 武皇渡汴，遇賊將渡而南，半濟擊之，大敗之，臨陣斬賊將李周、王濟安、陽景彪等。
units.en: He crossed the Bian, caught rebel columns mid-river, cut them down, and killed Li Zhou, Wang Ji'an, and Yang Jingbiao in the fighting.
units.literal: Wuhuang crossed the Bian, met bandit generals crossing south, struck them halfway across, routed them utterly, and on the field beheaded the bandit generals Li Zhou, Wang Ji'an, and Yang Jingbiao.

units.zh: 是夜，賊大敗，殘眾保於胙縣、冤句。
units.en: That night the rebels were shattered; the remnants held Zuo county and Yuanqu.
units.literal: That night the bandits were crushed; the survivors held Zuo county and Yuanqu.

units.zh: 大軍躡之，黃巢乃攜妻子兄弟千餘人東走，武皇追賊至於曹州。
units.en: The pursuit closed in; Huang Chao fled east with more than a thousand kin; Wuhuang chased him as far as Cao prefecture.
units.literal: The main army pressed them; Huang Chao then took his wife, children, and brothers—a thousand and more—and fled east; Wuhuang pursued the bandits to Cao prefecture.

units.zh: 是月，班師過汴，汴帥迎勞於封禪寺，請武皇休於府第，乃以從官三百人及監軍使陳景思館於上源驛。
units.en: On the homeward march that month he stopped at Bian; the Bian commander entertained him at Fengchan Temple and invited him to his residence while three hundred staff and the supervisor Chen Jingsi were lodged at Shangyuan Post.
units.literal: That month, on the return march he passed Bian; the Bian commander welcomed and feasted him at Fengchan Temple and asked Wuhuang to rest at his mansion, lodging his three hundred followers and the army supervisor Chen Jingsi at Shangyuan Post.

units.zh: 是夜，張樂陳宴席，汴帥自佐饗，出珍幣侑勸。
units.en: That night there was a banquet with music; the Bian commander waited on him in person and offered costly gifts with the wine.
units.literal: That night music was arranged and a banquet set out; the Bian commander himself attended the feast and produced rare gifts to urge toasts.

units.zh: 武皇酒酣，戲諸侍妓，與汴帥握手，敘破賊事以為樂。
units.en: Drunk, Wuhuang bantered with the singing girls, clasped the Bian commander's hand, and exulted over their victory over the rebels.
units.literal: Wuhuang, flushed with wine, jested with the attendant women, clasped the Bian commander's hand, and took pleasure in recounting how they had broken the bandits.

units.zh: 汴帥素忌武皇，乃與其將楊彥洪密謀竊發，彥洪於巷陌連車樹柵，以扼奔竄之路。
units.en: The Bian commander had long envied him; he and Yang Yanhong plotted a night attack and barricaded the streets with chained carts.
units.literal: The Bian commander had long resented Wuhuang; he and his general Yang Yanhong secretly plotted a surprise attack, and Yanhong lined carts in the lanes and set barriers to block escape.

units.zh: 時武皇之從官皆醉，俄而伏兵竄發，來攻傳舍。
units.en: Wuhuang's party was drunk when ambushers stormed the lodge.
units.literal: At the time Wuhuang's attendants were all drunk; suddenly hidden troops burst forth and attacked the lodge.

units.zh: 武皇方大醉，噪聲動地，從官十餘人捍賊。
units.en: Still heavily drunk, he heard the clamor; a dozen followers fought off the attackers.
units.literal: Wuhuang was deep in wine; the uproar shook the earth, and a dozen or so attendants fought the bandits.

units.zh: 侍人郭景銖滅燭扶武皇，以茵幕裹之，匿於床下，以水灑麵，徐曰：「汴帥謀害司空！」
units.en: Guo Jingzhu put out the lamps, steadied Wuhuang, wrapped him in bedding, hid him beneath the couch, splashed water on his face, and whispered: "The Bian commander means to murder you, Minister of Works!"
units.literal: The attendant Guo Jingzhu extinguished the lamps, supported Wuhuang, wrapped him in a curtain, hid him under the bed, sprinkled water on his face, and said slowly: "The Bian commander plots to kill the Minister of Works!"

units.zh: 武皇方張目而起，引弓抗賊。
units.en: He opened his eyes, got up, and shot back at the assailants.
units.literal: Wuhuang then opened his eyes, rose, and drew his bow against the bandits.

units.zh: 有頃，煙火四合，復大雨震電，武皇得從者薛鐵山、賀回鶻等數人而去。
units.en: Fire closed in on every side; thunder and rain broke again; he escaped with Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and a few others.
units.literal: Before long fire blazed on every side; again great rain, thunder, and lightning; Wuhuang escaped with several followers including Xue Tieshan and He Huihu.

units.zh: 雨水如澍，不辨人物，隨電光登尉氏門，縋城而出，得還本營。
units.en: Rain fell in sheets and men could not see one another; by a flash of lightning he scaled Weishi Gate, was let down by rope, and reached his camp.
units.literal: The rain poured like a flood; men could not be told apart; by lightning he climbed Weishi Gate, was lowered from the wall by rope, and returned to his own camp.

units.zh: 監軍陳景思、大將史敬思並遇害。
units.en: Chen Jingsi, the army supervisor, and the general Shi Jingsi were killed.
units.literal: The army supervisor Chen Jingsi and the great general Shi Jingsi were both killed.

units.zh: 武皇既還營，與劉夫人相向慟哭。
units.en: Back in camp he and Lady Liu wept together.
units.literal: Once Wuhuang was back in camp, he and Lady Liu wept face to face.

units.zh: 詰旦，欲勒軍攻汴，夫人曰：「司空比為國家討賊，赴東諸侯之急，雖汴人謀害，自有朝廷論列。
units.en: At dawn he wanted to turn the army on Bian; Lady Liu said: "You have just served the throne against the rebels and hurried east at the other lords' call; if Bian plotted against you, the court will judge it.
units.literal: At dawn he wished to marshal the army against Bian; the lady said: "The Minister of Works has lately served the state in exterminating bandits and rushed east to relieve the other lords; though the men of Bian plotted against you, the court itself will judge the matter.

units.zh: 若反戈攻城，則曲在我也，人得以為辭。」
units.en: If you attack their city, the fault will be yours and they will have a case against you."
units.literal: If you turn your blades to storm a city, the wrong will be on our side, and others will have grounds to speak against you."

units.zh: 乃收軍而去，馳檄於汴帥。
units.en: He drew off the army and sent an urgent message to the Bian commander.
units.literal: He then withdrew the army and sent a rapid dispatch to the Bian commander.

units.zh: 汴帥報曰：「竊發之夜，非仆本心，是朝廷遣天使與牙將楊彥洪同謀也。」
units.en: The Bian commander answered: "I did not intend that night's attack; an imperial envoy from the court plotted it with Yang Yanhong."
units.literal: The Bian commander replied: "On the night of the surprise attack it was not my own intent; the court sent an imperial envoy who plotted together with the military commissioner Yang Yanhong."

units.zh: 武皇自武牢關西趨蒲、陝而旋。
units.en: Wuhuang marched west through Wulao Pass by way of Pu and Shan and withdrew.
units.literal: Wuhuang went west through Wulao Pass toward Pu and Shan and returned.

units.zh: 秋七月，至太原。
units.en: In the seventh month of autumn he reached Taiyuan.
units.literal: Autumn, seventh month, he reached Taiyuan.

units.zh: 武皇自以累立大功，為汴帥怨圖，陷沒諸將，乃上章申理。
units.en: Feeling that his repeated victories had been repaid with the Bian commander's treachery and the death of his officers, he memorialized the throne.
units.literal: Wuhuang, considering that he had repeatedly achieved great merit yet been plotted against by the Bian commander with the loss of many generals, submitted a memorial to state his case.

units.zh: 及武皇表至，朝廷大恐，遣內臣宣諭，尋加守太傅、同平章事、隴西郡王。
units.en: The court was alarmed when his memorial arrived, sent an inner envoy to reassure him, and soon made him Grand Tutor, Tongping Grand Councilor, and Duke of Longxi.
units.literal: When Wuhuang's memorial arrived the court was greatly alarmed, sent an inner courtier to soothe him with edicts, and soon added Grand Tutor, Tongping Grand Councilor, and Duke of Longxi.

units.zh: 光啟元年三月，幽州李可舉、鎮州王景崇連兵寇定州，節度使王處存求援於武皇；
units.en: In the third month of Guangqi 1, Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou jointly attacked Ding Prefecture; Wang Chucun, the military commissioner, appealed to Wuhuang for aid;
units.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guangqi, Li Keju of Youzhou and Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou jointly marched to raid Ding Prefecture; military commissioner Wang Chucun sought aid from Wuhuang;

units.zh: 武皇遣大將康君立、安老、薛可、郭啜率兵赴之。
units.en: Wuhuang sent Kang Junli, An Lao, Xue Ke, and Guo Chuo with troops to the rescue.
units.literal: Wuhuang sent the great generals Kang Junli, An Lao, Xue Ke, and Guo Chuo with troops to go to the relief.

units.zh: 五月，鎮人攻無極，武皇親領兵救之。
units.en: In the fifth month the Zhen troops attacked Wuji; Wuhuang led the army in person to relieve it.
units.literal: In the fifth month the men of Zhen attacked Wuji; Wuhuang personally led troops to the rescue.

units.zh: 鎮人退保新城，武皇攻之，斬首萬餘級，獲馬千匹。
units.en: The Zhen troops fell back to Xincheng; Wuhuang stormed the place, took more than ten thousand heads, and seized a thousand horses.
units.literal: The men of Zhen fell back to defend Xincheng; Wuhuang attacked them, beheaded more than ten thousand, and captured a thousand horses.

units.zh: 王處存亦敗燕軍於易州。
units.en: Wang Chucun also routed the Yan army at Yizhou.
units.literal: Wang Chucun also defeated the Yan army at Yi Prefecture.

units.zh: 十一月，河中王重榮遣使來乞師，且言邠州朱玫、鳳翔李符將加兵於己。
units.en: In the eleventh month Wang Chongrong of Hezhong asked for aid, saying Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Fu of Fengxiang were marching against him.
units.literal: Eleventh month, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong sent envoys begging for troops and reporting that Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Fu of Fengxiang were about to add troops against him.

units.zh: 初，武皇與汴人構怨，前後八表，請削奪汴帥官爵，自以本軍進討。
units.en: Already bitter toward Bian, Wuhuang had eight times asked that Zhu Wen be degraded and that he be allowed to attack him.
units.literal: Earlier, because of his feud with the men of Bian, Wuhuang had eight times memorialized asking that the Bian commander's titles be stripped and that he himself lead his army in punishment.

units.zh: 天子累遣內臣楊復恭宣旨，令且全大體，武皇不時奉詔，天子頗右汴帥。
units.en: The emperor repeatedly sent Yang Fugong to urge restraint; Wuhuang delayed obeying, and the court leaned toward Bian.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven repeatedly sent the inner courtier Yang Fugong to announce edicts telling him to preserve the larger settlement; Wuhuang did not promptly obey, and the Son of Heaven rather favored the Bian commander.

units.zh: 時觀軍容使田令孜君側擅權，惡王重榮與武皇膠固，將離其勢，乃移重榮於定州。
units.en: Tian Lingzi, the army supervisor, hated the alliance of Chongrong and Wuhuang and tried to split them by moving Chongrong to Dingzhou.
units.literal: At the time the army supervisor Tian Lingzi wielded power at the ruler's side, hated the close bond between Wang Chongrong and Wuhuang, and wished to break their strength, so he transferred Chongrong to Ding prefecture.

units.zh: 重榮告於武皇，武皇上章言：「李符、朱玫挾邪忌正，黨庇朱溫。
units.en: Chongrong appealed to Wuhuang, who wrote: "Li Fu and Zhu Mei are corrupt, hate the loyal, and protect Zhu Wen.
units.literal: Chongrong informed Wuhuang; Wuhuang memorialized: "Li Fu and Zhu Mei harbor evil, hate the upright, and shield Zhu Wen.

units.zh: 臣已點檢蕃漢軍五萬，取來年渡河，先斬朱玫、李冒符，然後平蕩朱溫。」
units.en: I have fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops ready and will cross the river next year, kill Zhu Mei and Li Fu, and then destroy Zhu Wen."
units.literal: Your subject has mustered fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops and will cross the river next year, first behead Zhu Mei and Li Mao-fu, and then sweep away Zhu Wen."

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·王重榮傳》：詔克用將兵援河中，重榮貽克用書，且言：「奉密詔，須公到，使我圖公，此令孜、朱全忠、朱玫之惑上也。」
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Wang Chongrong》 says: When Li Keyong was ordered to aid Hezhong, Chongrong wrote to him saying, "I have received a secret edict that, once you arrive, I am to plot against you—this is the deception Tian Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei have worked upon the throne."
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Wang Chongrong》 says: An edict ordered Li Keyong to lead troops to aid Hezhong; Chongrong sent Keyong a letter saying: "I have received a secret edict that, once you arrive, I am to plot against you—this is the deception of Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei at the court's ear."

units.zh: 因示偽詔。
units.en: He showed the forged edict as proof.
units.literal: He then showed the forged edict.

units.zh: 克用方與全忠有隙，信之，請討全忠及玫。）〉
units.en: Keyong, already hostile to Zhu Quanzhong, believed him and asked to attack Quanzhong and Mei.)〉
units.literal: Keyong was then at odds with Quanzhong, believed it, and asked permission to attack Quanzhong and Mei.)〉

units.zh: 天子覽表，遣使譬喻百端，軺傳相望。
units.en: The emperor read the memorial and sent envoy after envoy to reason with him; dispatches crowded the road.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven read the memorial and sent envoys to explain in a hundred ways; relay-chariots followed one another.

units.zh: 既而朱玫引邠、鳳之師攻河中，王重榮出師拒戰。
units.en: Soon Zhu Mei brought the Bin and Fengxiang armies against Hezhong and Chongrong marched out to meet them.
units.literal: Before long Zhu Mei led the Bin and Fengxiang armies against Hezhong; Wang Chongrong marched out to resist.

units.zh: 朱玫軍於沙苑，對壘月餘。
units.en: Zhu Mei camped at Shayuan and the armies faced each other for over a month.
units.literal: Zhu Mei's army encamped at Shayuan; the two sides faced each other for more than a month.

units.zh: 十二月，武皇引軍渡河，與朱玫決戰，玫大敗，收軍夜遁，入於京師。
units.en: In the twelfth month Wuhuang crossed the river, routed Zhu Mei in a decisive battle, and Mei fled by night into the capital.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang led troops across the river, fought Zhu Mei to the decision, Mei was utterly defeated, drew off the army and fled by night, and entered the capital.

units.zh: 時京城大駭。
units.en: The capital was thrown into panic.
units.literal: At the time the capital was in great alarm.

units.zh: 天子幸鳳翔，武皇退軍於河中。
units.en: The emperor fled to Fengxiang; Wuhuang pulled back to Hezhong.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven fled to Fengxiang; Wuhuang withdrew the army to Hezhong.

units.zh: 光啟二年正月，僖宗駐蹕於寶雞，武皇自河中遣使上章，請車駕還京，且言大軍止誅凶黨。
units.en: In the first month of Guangqi 2, with Xizong at Baoji, Wuhuang wrote from Hezhong asking him to return to Chang'an and promising to punish only the rebels.
units.literal: First month of the second year of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong halted at Baoji; Wuhuang from Hezhong sent envoys with a memorial asking that the imperial carriage return to the capital and stating that his great army would punish only the evil clique.

units.zh: 時田令孜請僖宗南幸興元，武皇遂班師。
units.en: Tian Lingzi persuaded Xizong to go south to Xingyuan, and Wuhuang withdrew.
units.literal: At the time Tian Lingzi urged Xizong to go south to Xingyuan; Wuhuang then withdrew the army.

units.zh: 朱玫於鳳翔立嗣襄王煴為帝，以偽詔賜武皇，武皇燔之，械其使，馳檄諸方鎮，遣使奉表於行在。
units.en: Zhu Mei set up Li Yun, Prince of Xiang, as emperor at Fengxiang and sent a forged edict to Wuhuang; Wuhuang burned it, chained the envoy, notified the provinces, and wrote to the traveling court.
units.literal: Zhu Mei at Fengxiang enthroned the heir Prince of Xiang Li Yun as emperor, sent a forged edict to bestow on Wuhuang; Wuhuang burned it, put the envoy in fetters, issued proclamations to the regional commands, and sent envoys with a loyal memorial to the traveling court.

units.zh: 九月，武皇遣昭義節度使李克修討孟方立於邢州，大敗方立之眾於焦崗，斬首數千級。
units.en: In the ninth month he sent Li Kexiu of Zhaoyi against Meng Fangli at Xingzhou; at Jiaogang Kexiu routed Fangli and took several thousand heads.
units.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang sent the Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Kexiu to attack Meng Fangli at Xing prefecture; at Jiaogang he crushed Fangli's host, beheading several thousand.

units.zh: 以大將安金俊為邢州刺史，以撫其降人。
units.en: He installed the general An Jinjun as prefect of Xing to pacify the surrendered.
units.literal: He made the great general An Jinjun prefect of Xing and used him to pacify those who surrendered.

units.zh: 十月，進攻邢州，邢人出戰，又敗之。
units.en: In the tenth month he besieged Xing; the defenders sallied and were beaten again.
units.literal: Tenth month, he pressed the attack on Xing; the Xing men came out to fight and were again defeated.

units.zh: 盂方立求援於鎮州，鎮人出兵三萬以援方立，克修班師。
units.en: Meng Fangli called on Zhenzhou for help; thirty thousand men came to his aid and Kexiu withdrew.
units.literal: Meng Fangli begged aid from Zhen prefecture; the Zhen men sent thirty thousand to relieve Fangli, and Kexiu withdrew the army.

units.zh: 光啟三年六月，河中節度使王重榮為部將常行儒所殺，武皇表重榮兄重盈為帥。
units.en: In the sixth month of Guangqi 3 the Hezhong commissioner Wang Chongrong was murdered by his officer Chang Xingru; Wuhuang asked that his brother Chongying succeed him.
units.literal: Sixth month of the third year of Guangqi, Wang Chongrong, military commissioner of Hezhong, was killed by his officer Chang Xingru; Wuhuang memorialized that Chongrong's elder brother Chongying be made commander.

units.zh: 七月，武皇以安金俊為澤州刺史。
units.en: In the seventh month he made An Jinjun prefect of Ze.
units.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang made An Jinjun prefect of Ze.

units.zh: 時張全義自河陽據澤州，及李罕之收復河陽，召全義令守洛陽，全義乃棄澤州而去，故以金俊守之。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi had seized Ze from Heyang; when Li Hanzhi retook Heyang he called Quanyi to Luoyang, Quanyi abandoned Ze, and Jinjun was stationed there.
units.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi held Ze prefecture from Heyang; when Li Hanzhi recovered Heyang he summoned Quanyi to guard Luoyang, and Quanyi abandoned Ze prefecture and left, so Jinjun was put to guard it.

units.zh: 文德元年二月，僖宗自興元還京。
units.en: In the second month of Wende 1, Emperor Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan.
units.literal: In the second month of the first year of Wende, Emperor Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan.

units.zh: 三月，僖宗崩，昭宗即位，以武皇為開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼侍中、隴西郡王，食邑七千戶，食實封二百戶。
units.en: In the third month Xizong died and Zhaozong succeeded; Wuhuang was made open-office commissioner with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, honorary Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, and Duke of Longxi, with a fief of seven thousand households and two hundred enfeoffed households.
units.literal: In the third month Xizong died and Zhaozong took the throne; Wuhuang was made commissioner with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, honorary Grand Tutor, concurrent Palace Attendant, Duke of Longxi, with a fief of seven thousand households and two hundred enfeoffed households.

units.zh: 河南尹張全義潛兵夜襲李罕之於河陽，城陷，舉族為全義所擄；
units.en: Zhang Quanyi, Henan governor, sent troops by night to surprise Li Hanzhi at Heyang; the city fell and Quanyi carried off his whole clan;
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, governor of Henan, secretly sent troops by night to surprise Li Hanzhi at Heyang; the city fell and his whole clan was carried off by Quanyi;

units.zh: 罕之逾垣獲免，遂來歸於武皇。
units.en: Hanzhi climbed a wall and escaped, then came to Wuhuang.
units.literal: Hanzhi climbed over a wall and escaped, then came to submit to Wuhuang.

units.zh: 遣李存孝、薛阿檀、史儼兒、安金俊、安休休將七千騎送罕之至河陽。
units.en: He sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, Shi Yan'er, An Jinjun, and An Xiuxiu with seven thousand horsemen to escort Hanzhi to Heyang.
units.literal: He sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, Shi Yan'er, An Jinjun, and An Xiuxiu with seven thousand horsemen to escort Hanzhi back to Heyang.

units.zh: 汴將丁會、牛存節、葛從周將兵赴援，李存孝率精騎逆戰於溫縣。
units.en: The Bian generals Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and Ge Congzhou marched to the relief; Li Cunxiao met them with picked cavalry at Wen County.
units.literal: The Bian generals Ding Hui, Niu Cunjie, and Ge Congzhou led troops to the relief; Li Cunxiao led picked cavalry to meet them in battle at Wen County.

units.zh: 汴人既扼太行之路，存孝殿軍而退。
units.en: With the Bian forces blocking the Taihang road, Cunxiao covered the retreat and withdrew.
units.literal: The men of Bian having blocked the Taihang route, Cunxiao covered the rear and withdrew.

units.zh: 騎將安休休以戰不利，奔於蔡。
units.en: The cavalry commander An Xiuxiu, fearing defeat, fled to Cai.
units.literal: The mounted commander An Xiuxiu, because the battle went badly, fled to Cai.

units.zh: 武皇以罕之為澤州刺史，遙領河陽節度使。
units.en: Wuhuang made Hanzhi prefect of Ze and titular commissioner of Heyang.
units.literal: Wuhuang made Hanzhi prefect of Ze and titular military commissioner of Heyang.

units.zh: 十月，邢州孟方立遣大將奚忠信將兵三萬寇遼州，武皇大破之，斬首萬級，生擒奚忠信。
units.en: In the tenth month Meng Fangli of Xingzhou sent Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops against Liaozhou; Wuhuang crushed them, took ten thousand heads, and captured Xi Zhongxin alive.
units.literal: In the tenth month Meng Fangli of Xing Prefecture sent the great general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to raid Liaozhou; Wuhuang routed them, beheaded ten thousand, and captured Xi Zhongxin alive.

units.zh: 龍紀元年五月，遣李罕之、李存孝攻邢州。
units.en: In the fifth month of Longji 1 he sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou.
units.literal: Fifth month of the first year of Longji, he sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to attack Xing prefecture.

units.zh: 六月，下磁州。
units.en: In the sixth month they took Cizhou.
units.literal: Sixth month, they took Ci prefecture.

units.zh: 邢將馬溉率兵數萬來拒戰，罕之敗之於琉璃陂，生擒馬溉，徇於城下。
units.en: Ma Gai of Xing brought tens of thousands to the fight; Hanzhi beat him at Liuli Slope, took him alive, and paraded him before the city.
units.literal: The Xing general Ma Gai led tens of thousands to resist; Hanzhi defeated him at Liuli Slope, captured Ma Gai alive, and displayed him below the walls.

units.zh: 孟方立恚恨，飲鴆而死。
units.en: Meng Fangli, in despair, took poison and died.
units.literal: Meng Fangli, resentful and enraged, drank poison and died.

units.zh: 三軍立其侄遷為留後，使求援於汴。
units.en: The army made his nephew Qian acting commander and asked Bian for help.
units.literal: The three armies installed his nephew Qian as acting commander and sent to Bian for aid.

units.zh: 汴將王虔裕率精甲數百入於邢州，罕之等班師。
units.en: Wang Qianyu of Bian entered Xing with several hundred elite horsemen; Hanzhi withdrew.
units.literal: The Bian general Wang Qianyu led several hundred picked horsemen into Xing prefecture; Hanzhi and the others withdrew the army.

units.zh: 大順元年，遣李存孝攻邢州，孟遷以邢、洺、磁三州降，執汴將王虔裕三百人以獻。
units.en: In Datong 1 he sent Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou; Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Cizhou and presented three hundred Bian prisoners led by Wang Qianyu.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong, he sent Li Cunxiao to attack Xing Prefecture; Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and presented three hundred Bian captives led by Wang Qianyu.

units.zh: 武皇徙孟遷於太原，以安金俊為邢洺團練使。
units.en: Wuhuang moved Meng Qian to Taiyuan and made An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.
units.literal: Wuhuang moved Meng Qian to Taiyuan and made An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.

units.zh: 三月，昭義軍節度使李克修卒，以李克恭為潞州節度使。
units.en: In the third month Zhaoyi commissioner Li Kexiu died, and Li Kegong was made military commissioner of Luzhou.
units.literal: In the third month Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Kexiu died, and Li Kegong was made military commissioner of Lu Prefecture.

units.zh: 是月，武皇攻雲州，拔其東城。
units.en: That month Wuhuang attacked Yunzhou and captured its eastern quarter.
units.literal: That month Wuhuang attacked Yun Prefecture and took its eastern city.

units.zh: 赫連鐸求援於燕，燕帥李匡威將兵三萬以赴之，戰於城下，燕軍大敗。
units.en: Helian Duo appealed to Yan; the Yan commander Li Kuangwei marched thirty thousand men to his aid; they fought below the walls and the Yan army was routed.
units.literal: Helian Duo sought aid from Yan; the Yan commander Li Kuangwei led thirty thousand troops to go to the relief; they fought below the walls and the Yan army was routed.

units.zh: 時徐州時溥為汴軍所攻，遣使來求援，武皇命石君和由兗、鄆以赴之。
units.en: Shi Pu of Xuzhou was then under attack by Bian; he sent envoys begging for aid, and Wuhuang ordered Shi Junhe to march from Yan and Yun to relieve him.
units.literal: At the time Shi Pu of Xuzhou was attacked by the Bian army; he sent envoys begging for aid, and Wuhuang ordered Shi Junhe to go by way of Yan and Yun to the relief.

units.zh: 五月，潞州軍亂，殺節度使李克恭，州人推牙將安居受為留後，南結汴將。
units.en: In the fifth month the Lu garrison killed commissioner Li Kegong; the men made the junior officer An Jushou acting commander and turned to Bian.
units.literal: Fifth month, the Lu army mutinied, killed the military commissioner Li Kegong, and the prefectural men pushed the junior officer An Jushou as acting commander, allying south with the Bian commander.

units.zh: 時潞之小將馮霸擁叛徒三千騎駐於沁水，居受使人召之，馮霸不至。
units.en: Feng Ba, a Lu officer, held three thousand mutinous horsemen at Qinshui; Jushou summoned him, but he refused.
units.literal: At the time the Lu junior officer Feng Ba held three thousand rebel horsemen at Qinshui; Jushou sent men to summon him, but Feng Ba did not come.

units.zh: 居受懼，出奔至長子，為村胥所殺，傳首於霸；
units.en: Jushou fled in fear to Changzi, where a village headman killed him and sent his head to Feng Ba;
units.literal: Jushou was afraid, fled to Changzi, and was killed by a village headman, who sent his head to Feng Ba;

units.zh: 霸遂入潞州，自為留後。
units.en: Feng Ba then entered Lu and declared himself acting commander.
units.literal: Feng Ba then entered Lu prefecture and made himself acting commander.

units.zh: 武皇遣大將康君立、李存孝等攻之，汴將朱崇節、葛從周率兵入潞州以固之。
units.en: Wuhuang sent Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao against him; Zhu Chongjie and Ge Congzhou of Bian marched into Lu to hold the city.
units.literal: Wuhuang sent the great generals Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao to attack him; the Bian generals Zhu Chongjie and Ge Congzhou led troops into Lu prefecture to reinforce it.

units.zh: 是時，幽州李匡威、雲州赫連鐸與汴帥協謀，連上表請加兵於太原，宰相張浚、孔緯讚成其事。
units.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou joined Zhu Wen in urging the court to reinforce the campaign against Taiyuan; Zhang Jun and Kong Wei backed them.
units.literal: At the time Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou plotted with the Bian commander, jointly memorializing again and again to add troops against Taiyuan; the chancellors Zhang Jun and Kong Wei approved the plan.

units.zh: 六月，天子削奪武皇官爵，以張浚為招討使，以京兆尹孫揆為副，華州韓建為行營都虞候，以汴帥為河東南面招討使，幽州李匡威為河東北面招討使，雲州赫連鐸為副。
units.en: In the sixth month the emperor degraded Wuhuang, made Zhang Jun commander of the expedition with Sun Kui as deputy and Han Jian as chief of staff, Zhu Wen southern commissioner against Hedong, Li Kuangwei northern commissioner, and Helian Duo his deputy.
units.literal: Sixth month, the Son of Heaven stripped Wuhuang of rank and office, made Zhang Jun commander of the punitive campaign and Sun Kui of the capital auxiliary, Han Jian of Huazhou chief of staff of the field army, the Bian commander southern punitive commissioner against Hedong, Li Kuangwei of Youzhou northern punitive commissioner against Hedong, and Helian Duo of Yunzhou his deputy.

units.zh: 汴將朱友裕將兵屯晉、絳，時汴軍已據潞州，又遣大將李讜等率軍數萬，急攻澤州，武皇遣李存孝自潞州將三千騎以援之。
units.en: Zhu Youyu of Bian encamped at Jin and Jiang; Bian already held Lu, and Li Dang and others were hurrying tens of thousands against Ze; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve the city.
units.literal: The Bian general Zhu Youyu led troops to camp at Jin and Jiang; by then the Bian army already held Lu prefecture, and he also sent the great general Li Dang and others with tens of thousands to press the attack on Ze prefecture; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve it.

units.zh: 汴將鄧季筠以一軍犯陣，存孝追擊，擒其都將十數人，獲馬千餘匹。
units.en: Bian general Deng Jiyun led a detachment against the line; Li Cunxiao pursued, took a dozen of his commanders, and captured more than a thousand horses.
units.literal: Bian general Deng Jiyun led one army to strike the formation; Cunxiao pursued, captured more than ten of his commanders, and seized over a thousand horses.

units.zh: 是夜，李讜收軍而退，大軍掩擊至馬牢關，斬首萬餘級，追襲至懷州而還。
units.en: That night Li Dang pulled back; the main army struck in pursuit to Malao Pass, took more than ten thousand heads, and chased as far as Huai Prefecture before turning back.
units.literal: That night Li Dang withdrew his army; the main force ambushed in pursuit to Malao Pass, beheaded more than ten thousand, and pursued as far as Huai Prefecture before returning.

units.zh: 存孝復引軍攻潞州。
units.en: Cunxiao again marched on Lu Prefecture.
units.literal: Cunxiao again led troops to attack Lu Prefecture.

units.zh: 八月，存孝擒新授昭義節度使孫揆。
units.en: In the eighth month Li Cunxiao captured the newly appointed Zhaoyi military commissioner Sun Kui.
units.literal: In the eighth month Cunxiao captured the newly appointed Zhaoyi military commissioner Sun Kui.

units.zh: 初，朝廷授揆節鉞，以本軍取刀黃嶺路赴任，存孝偵知之，引騎三百伏於長子縣崖穀間。
units.en: The court had given Kui his commission and ordered him to take his troops by the Daohuang Ridge road to his post. Cunxiao learned of it, led three hundred cavalry, and hid in the cliff gorges of Changzi.
units.literal: At first the court invested Kui with credentials; he was to take his own troops by the Daohuang Ridge route to his post. Cunxiao learned of it and led three hundred horsemen to lie in ambush in the cliff ravines of Changzi county.

units.zh: 揆建牙持節，褒衣大蓋，擁眾而行，存孝突出穀口，遂擒揆及中使韓歸範，並將校五百人。
units.en: Kui went forth with his insignia, broad robes, and a great canopy, surrounded by his train. Cunxiao rushed from the gorge, seized Kui and the palace envoy Han Guifan, and five hundred officers and men.
units.literal: Kui raised his command standard with credentials, wore broad robes and a great canopy, and marched with a large retinue. Cunxiao burst from the ravine mouth, captured Kui and the palace envoy Han Guifan, and five hundred officers and troops.

units.zh: 存孝械揆等，以組練係之，環於潞州，遂獻於武皇。
units.en: Cunxiao put Kui and the rest in fetters, tied them with cords, paraded them around Lu Prefecture, and sent them to Wuhuang.
units.literal: Cunxiao shackled Kui and the others, bound them with silk cords, displayed them around Lu Prefecture, and then presented them to Wuhuang.

units.zh: 武皇謂揆曰：「公搢紳之士，安言徐步可至達官，何用如是！」
units.en: Wuhuang told Kui, "You are a court gentleman; they say a man need only walk slowly to reach high rank—why trouble yourself like this!"
units.literal: Wuhuang said to Kui: "You are a court gentleman—who says slow steps cannot reach high office? Why go to such lengths!"

units.zh: 揆無以對，令係於晉陽獄。
units.en: Kui could not answer and was confined in the Jinyang prison.
units.literal: Kui had no reply; he was ordered confined in the Jinyang prison.

units.zh: 武皇將用為副使，使人誘之，揆言不遜，遂殺之。
units.en: Wuhuang meant to make him his deputy and sent men to win him over; Kui answered insolently and was executed.
units.literal: Wuhuang intended to use him as deputy, sent men to win him over; Kui's words were insolent, and he was put to death.

units.zh: 九月，汴將葛從周棄潞州而遁，武皇以康君立為潞州節度使，以李存孝為汾州刺史。
units.en: In the ninth month Ge Congzhou of Bian abandoned Lu and fled. Wuhuang made Kang Junli military commissioner of Lu and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen.
units.literal: In the ninth month Bian general Ge Congzhou abandoned Lu Prefecture and fled. Wuhuang made Kang Junli military commissioner of Lu and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen.

units.zh: 十月，張浚之師入晉州，遊軍至汾、隰。
units.en: In the tenth month Zhang Jun's army entered Jin Prefecture and scouting parties reached Fen and Xi.
units.literal: In the tenth month Zhang Jun's army entered Jin Prefecture; patrol troops reached Fen and Xi.

units.zh: 武皇遣薛鐵山、李承嗣將騎三千出陰地關，營於洪洞，遣李存孝將兵五千，營於趙城。
units.en: Wuhuang sent Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi with three thousand horse out Yindi Pass to camp at Hongdong, and Li Cunxiao with five thousand men to camp at Zhaocheng.
units.literal: Wuhuang sent Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi with three thousand cavalry out through Yindi Pass to camp at Hongdong, and Li Cunxiao with five thousand troops to camp at Zhaocheng.

units.zh: 華州韓建以壯士三百人冒犯存孝之營，存孝追擊，直壓晉州西門，張浚之師出戰，為存孝所敗，自是閉壁不出。
units.en: Han Jian of Huazhou sent three hundred picked men against Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao pursued them to the west gate of Jin Prefecture. When Zhang Jun's army came out to fight, Cunxiao routed it; from then on they shut the walls and would not come out.
units.literal: Han Jian of Huazhou led three hundred stalwarts against Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao pursued, pressed straight to the west gate of Jin Prefecture; Zhang Jun's army came out to fight and was defeated by Cunxiao—after that they closed the walls and did not emerge.

units.zh: 存孝引軍攻絳州。
units.en: Cunxiao marched on Jiang Prefecture.
units.literal: Cunxiao led troops to attack Jiang Prefecture.

units.zh: 十二月，晉州刺史張行恭棄城而奔，韓建、張浚由含山路遁去。
units.en: In the twelfth month Jin prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Han Jian and Zhang Jun slipped away by the Hanshan road.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Jin prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Han Jian and Zhang Jun escaped by the Hanshan route.

units.zh: 大順二年春正月，武皇上章申理，其略曰：「臣今身無官爵，名是罪人，不敢歸陛下藩方，且欲於河中寄寓，進退行止，伏候聖裁。」
units.en: In the first month of spring in Datong 2, Wuhuang memorialized in his own defense, saying in summary: "Your servant now holds no office and bears the name of a criminal; I dare not return to my circuit under Your Majesty and wish instead to lodge at Hezhong for a time; my movements await the sacred decision."
units.literal: In spring, first month of Datong 2, Wuhuang memorialized in his own defense, in summary: "Your servant now has no office or rank and his name is that of a criminal; he dares not return to Your Majesty's border circuit, and wishes rather to lodge temporarily at Hezhong; whether to advance or withdraw, he awaits the sacred decision."

units.zh: 天子尋就加守中書令。
units.en: The emperor soon made him acting chief councilor.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven soon added to his titles Acting Chancellor of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：二月，復拜克用河東節度使、隴西郡王，加檢校太師、兼中書令。）〉
units.en: (Ouyang's history says: In the second month Keyong was again made military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi, with the added titles of honorary Grand Preceptor and chief councilor.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》: In the second month Keyong was again appointed military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi, and promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Chancellor of the Secretariat.)〉

units.zh: 是月，魏博為汴將葛從周所寇，節度使羅宏信遣使來求援，武皇出師以赴之。
units.en: That month Ge Congzhou of Bian raided Weibo; military commissioner Luo Hongxin sent envoys asking for help, and Wuhuang marched to relieve him.
units.literal: That month Weibo was raided by Bian general Ge Congzhou; military commissioner Luo Hongxin sent envoys to beg aid, and Wuhuang marched out to their relief.

units.zh: 三月，邢州節度使安知建叛，奔青州。
units.en: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.
units.literal: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.

units.zh: 天子以知建為神武統軍，自棣州溯河歸朝。
units.en: The emperor named him commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court up the river from Di Prefecture.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven made Zhijian commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court by river upstream from Di Prefecture.

units.zh: 鄆州朱瑄邀斬於河上，傳首晉陽。
units.en: Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou cut him down on the river and sent his head to Jinyang.
units.literal: Yanzhou's Zhu Xuan intercepted and beheaded him on the river, and sent the head to Jinyang.

units.zh: 以李存孝為邢州節度使。
units.en: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.
units.literal: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.

units.zh: 四月，武皇大舉兵討赫連鐸於雲州，遣騎將薛阿檀率前軍以進攻，武皇設伏兵於御河之上，大破之，因塹守其城。
units.en: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Duo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Duo utterly and then walled the city in.
units.literal: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army to attack Helian Duo at Yun Prefecture, sent cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to advance the assault; Wuhuang set ambush troops above the Yu River, routed them utterly, and thereby besieged the city with trenches.

units.zh: 七月，武皇進軍柳會，赫連鐸力屈食盡，奔於吐渾部，遂歸幽州，雲州平。
units.en: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, out of strength and food, fled to the Tuyuhun and then to Youzhou; Yunzhou was pacified.
units.literal: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, strength exhausted and provisions spent, fled to the Tuyuhun, then went to You Prefecture; Yun Prefecture was pacified.

units.zh: 武皇表石善友為大同軍防禦使。
units.en: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.
units.literal: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

units.zh: 邢州節度使李存孝以鎮州王熔托附汴人，謀亂河朔，北連燕寇，請乘雲、代之捷，平定燕、趙，武皇然之。
units.en: Li Cunxiao of Xing, seeing that Wang Rong of Zhen had thrown in with Bian, plotted to stir trouble in Hebei and ally with Yan in the north; he asked to use the Yun and Dai victories to pacify Yan and Zhao, and Wuhuang agreed.
units.literal: Xing military commissioner Li Cunxiao, because Zhen's Wang Rong had entrusted himself to Bian, plotted to throw Hebei into disorder and link with northern Yan raiders; he asked to use the victory at Yun and Dai to pacify Yan and Zhao; Wuhuang agreed.

units.zh: 八月，大搜於晉陽，遂南巡澤、潞，略地懷、孟，河陽趙克裕望風送款，請修鄰好。
units.en: In the eighth month he held a great hunt at Jinyang, then marched south through Ze and Lu and overran Huai and Meng; Zhao Keyu of Heyang submitted at his approach and asked for peace between neighbors.
units.literal: In the eighth month a great hunt was held at Jinyang; then he toured south through Ze and Lu, overran the lands of Huai and Meng; Heyang's Zhao Keyu submitted at the first rumor of his approach and asked for neighborly peace.

units.zh: 九月，蒐於邢州。
units.en: In the ninth month he hunted at Xingzhou.
units.literal: In the ninth month a hunt at Xing Prefecture.

units.zh: 十月，李存孝董前軍攻臨城，鎮人五萬營於臨城西北龍尾崗。
units.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao led the vanguard against Lincheng; fifty thousand men of Zhen camped on Longwei Ridge northwest of the city.
units.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao directed the vanguard to attack Lincheng; fifty thousand Zhen troops encamped at Longwei Ridge northwest of Lincheng.

units.zh: 武皇令李存審、李存賢以步軍攻之，鎮人大敗，殺獲萬計，拔臨城，進攻元氏。
units.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with infantry against them; the Zhen army was routed, with tens of thousands killed or taken; Lincheng fell and the attack moved on Yuanshi.
units.literal: Wuhuang ordered Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with foot troops to attack them; the Zhen army was badly defeated, with tens of thousands killed or captured; Lincheng was taken and the attack pressed on Yuanshi.

units.zh: 幽州李匡威以步騎五萬營於鄗邑，以援鎮州，武皇分兵大掠，旋軍邢州。
units.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou camped at Hao with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang split his forces for wide raiding and then wheeled back to Xingzhou.
units.literal: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei with fifty thousand foot and horse encamped at Hao town to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang divided his forces for wide plunder and then turned the army back to Xing.
